candidates.title: Measure usable context on more than a single retrieval needle
candidates.rule: Before setting a harness context budget, test retrieval, multi-hop tracing and aggregation at representative lengths and task complexities, then confirm on the actual workload.
candidates.passage: almost all models fail to maintain their performance in other tasks of Ruler as we increase input length.
candidates.finding: Seventeen historical models are tested on thirteen synthetic tasks. Near-perfect simple retrieval coexists with degradation on other tasks. The actionable budget-selection procedure is inferred; the paper does not test a production harness using it.
models: Llama3.1, Qwen2, Command-R-plus and other historical models
workloads: RULER synthetic retrieval, tracing, aggregation and QA
candidates.conditions: Lengths from 4K to 128K in the main comparison, with harder Yi tests up to 256K. Difficulty and irrelevant content vary.
candidates.limitations: The paper explicitly lacks demonstrated correlation with realistic long-context tasks and comprehensive prompt-robustness analysis. Its baseline threshold does not define universal acceptable quality or current model limits.
candidates.validation_test: For each target model, sweep context length and distractor load on representative tasks; track missing facts, aggregation errors and cost. Use synthetic tests as diagnostics and real held-out tasks for deployment decisions.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
